mascot.name: Pip
mascot.design: Our own small baby elephant (a nod to PHP's elePHPant, not the official mascot; built in src/lib/mascot): egg-shaped body, two big round ear flaps with salmon inners, a short curled trunk with 2-3 wrinkle ticks, a 3-strand head tuft, 3 downward-bowed back wrinkles (the cat's stripes), cream toenails, salmon soles, dot eyes, no tusks, no text, no logo. Loose 3.4 px ink with open contours (top of head between the ears and the base left open), flat fill offset 3 px right / 2 px down. Size: scale 1.0 (~96 px sitting) in the three vistas (S01, S08, S10 Part B) so his tininess is a peak effect; scale 1.2 (~115 px, reference 2's corgi size) in every medium and close scene so the small gags read on a phone; never below 0.75; in big camera moves he is kept at constant screen size (screen space). Plays the reference cat's role: perched, watching, reacting, one small physical gag per scene timed to its word (placed 0.25 s after the key word's focal event, near it), never covering the thing being explained, the sun or the counter. Exactly ONE look to camera in the film (S04 'right?'). Crosses every transition (hop, fall, ride). Poses used, all from docs/mascot.md: sit-back, sit-front, stand-side, walk-side, trunk-up, hold, ears-cover, sleep. Props: Flashlight (S09) and NewLock (S10) are authored by those scene builders in their own folders through the prop API; the S07 flyer is a scene overlay over the sit-front head bounds, not a prop; the S11 nod is a sit-back squash pulse. Supporting cast (not mascots): Bit, a solid-ink beetle (the bug: 16 px in wide shots, ~60 px in close-up) hiding in plain sight from frame 0 to the final frame; a sand-shelled snail (running gag S09-S11).
mascot.colorway: periwinkle #8D90CC body (shade per src/lib/mascot/colors.ts), salmon (= theme peach) ear inners, cheeks and soles, cream toenails, ink #2B1B0A. Periwinkle is reserved for Pip: no scene object ever uses it (PHP markers are sand plates with an ink elephant).

scenes.setting: STORY PEAK 1/3 (true Arcane-scale hook, 0-4.8 s). Government Plaza in Webtown, a city where every building is a website. Four monumental government buildings (four countries) at the far edge of a wide plaza, two on each side of a deep gap; the outer two are cropped by the frame edges so they read bigger than the frame. Through the gap: the far city and the horizon, with the huge low sun sitting in it. A flat sun path runs from the gap down the plaza to Pip. We stand low on the plaza among a few big back-view onlookers at the frame sides.

Day sky y 0-~900 (captions in it: theme skyCaption, baselines 387/510, clip 280-570; SKY CEILING: nothing but sky above screen y 560 inside x 90-990, so every roofline, spire and pennant tip sits at world y >= 600). A flat cream sun path (LightShaft, fixed opacity) from the gap down the plaza to Pip's bollard, with flat sage shadow wedges from govB and govD. Tiny citizens 40-55 px at y 1215-1300. beats.action: Frame 0 = loop seam state (see the transition notes). Camera push starts (4% over 2.2 s, then lock). The sun continues its rise (630,850)->(630,800), ease-out 0.37 s, then +7% pulse 0.30-0.55. Caption page 1 finishes its last 24 px of roll by 0.25.

'websites': chunky browser chrome reveals in all four main windows: tealDark title bars wipe on, three 15 px dots pop with overshoot (0.04 s stagger), cream address pills draw on (0.2 s); order govB, govA, govC, govD, 0.08 s apart. This is the 'building = website' teach.
Screens switch on: cream glow + peach page-header block + 3 ink hairlines pop inside each window (0.90-1.05).
'in': nine tiny citizens rise in on the plaza (0.33 s out(exp), 0.05 s stagger, left to right); the two in the sunPath are flat sage silhouettes.
'four': four pennants unfurl one per beat at 1.23 / 1.38 / 1.53 / 1.68 (scaleX 0->1, 6% overshoot), a counting tick each. Sun pulse +6% on 'four' (1.325).
Three pigeons land on the lamp crossbar (0.06 s stagger).
Two citizens raise phones (arm lines + white phones). Pip's ear flicks; he looks toward govB (look 0.3).
'just': the bold power glyph on the sun glints (two ink glint ticks) and the sun pulses +6%.
'switched': the sun is PRESSED like a power button (squash to 0.88 over 0.08 s, release 0.2 s) and one ink ripple ring expands from it (r150->190, 0.2 s). This press is the deliberate act.
Shutter 1 slams down over govA's browser window (0.16 s, 6 px bounce); govA steps one palette step darker as it lands.
'themselves': shutter 2 slams on govB, govB goes dark.
'-selves': shutter 3 slams on govC, govC goes dark (its clock face stays white).

'off': shutter 4 slams on govD, govD goes dark; the lamp lantern switches off (cream -> sand); the pigeons scatter (3.30); Pip startles: a quick trunk-up hop on the bollard (3.28-3.60, expression wide). The sunPath stays bright.

'Nobody': padlocks pop onto the four shutters at 3.64 / 3.72 / 3.80 / 3.88, each with a small click.
'hacked': Pip looks left, then right (look -0.6 -> 0.6), checking. No intruders anywhere; every door and wall is intact.

scenes.setting: STORY PEAK 3/3 (true Arcane-scale). Part A: Stoop Street in the morning, where one keeper installs the fix on door #4. scenes.composition: Part A (47.72-49.45) = the S03 set; an approach push to zoom 1.5 centred (330,900) lands the hero cornice at screen y 570 and lock4 at screen (540,1305), 51x63 px. Part B (49.45-54.46) = 'the hillside', canvas coords at rest: day sky above the ridge (y ~715). Terraces of frontal townhouse facades climb from the street to the ridge with NO overlap: row k has facade width w_k = 90*0.8^k, height h_k = 158*0.8^k, base_k = top_(k-1) - 3*0.8^k, so the bases are y 1500, 1339.6, 1211.3, 1108.7, 1026.7, 961.0, 908.6, 866.6, 833.0, 806.1, 784.6, 767.4, the ridge at ~715, and ~650 doors sit in rows 0-11 before the pattern tiling takes over. Thin retaining-wall lines and zig-zag stairs between the terraces, no roof planes, so it reads as looking UP a hill. Row 0 house #4 (the hidden-match object): facade x 482.5-572.5 (y 1342-1500), browser window x 500-555, y 1372-1407, door x 515-545, y 1439.5-1489.5, lock 8.5x10.5 centred (540,1464.5).
